name: North Macedonia
summary: Independent from Yugoslavia in 1991; renamed North Macedonia in 2019 after an agreement with Greece.

knownFor.label: Prespa Agreement
knownFor.note: Ended the name dispute with Greece.

terrain.value: Mountains around the Vardar River valley; Lake Ohrid and Lake Prespa.

climate.value: Continental, with hot summers and cold winters, and a Mediterranean influence in the south.

resources.value: Farmland (tobacco, vegetables, wine), lead, zinc and chrome.

disasters.value: An earthquake destroyed much of Skopje (1963).

urbanisation.value: About 58% urban; Skopje has about 600,000 people.

disease.value: Life expectancy is about 75 years, and health care is public.

migration.value: Many young people emigrate to Western Europe.

economicBase.value: An open, upper-middle-income economy with trade above 90% of GDP. Farming, car parts and textiles are not listed in the part of the page read.

tradeRoutes.value: The Vardar corridor between Central Europe and Greece.

inequality.value: High unemployment in some regions, especially among young people.

governmentType.value: A unitary parliamentary republic with a 120-seat Assembly; the prime minister holds most real power.

keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: North Macedonia; Britannica: North Macedonia, independence (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Kiro Gligorov was the first president and served until 1999)

succession.value: Governments change through elections; the president is elected directly.

institutions.value: Assembly (Sobranie); power-sharing with Albanians under the Ohrid Agreement (2001).

stability.value: A conflict between the government and ethnic Albanian insurgents from February to August 2001.

eliteConflict.value: Competition and cooperation between ethnic Macedonian and Albanian parties.

majorWars.value: Fighting between the government and ethnic Albanian insurgents ran from February to August 2001, ending with a NATO-monitored ceasefire and the Ohrid Agreement.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: North Macedonia (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: North Macedonia, independence (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Britannica says the 2001 conflict ended in August 2001 with the Ohrid Framework Agreement; it gives no February start date)

territoryChange.value: Renamed “North Macedonia” (2019) to end a dispute with Greece.

alliancesRivals.value: NATO member; EU candidate, delayed by disputes with Greece and Bulgaria.

scienceEducation.value: Ss. Cyril and Methodius University (1949); the medieval Ohrid Literary School.

openness.value: An open economy that seeks closer ties with the EU.

communicationTransport.value: Roads and rail follow the Vardar valley from Skopje to Greece.

languageWriting.value: Macedonian (in Cyrillic) is official, with Albanian used widely.

artsArchitecture.value: Medieval churches and icons of Ohrid; the Skopje 2014 statue project.

socialStructure.value: Macedonians and Albanians, with Turkish and Roma minorities.

sharedIdentity.value: Name and identity disputes with neighbours.

dailyLife.value: Houses and flats; ajvar, tavče gravče (baked beans).

ideasReligions.value: Orthodox Christianity is the main faith, with a large Muslim minority.

colonisation.value: Under Ottoman rule for about 500 years (1390s–1912); then part of Serbia and Yugoslavia.

riseSignals.value: A constituent state of communist Yugoslavia from 1945; independence is celebrated on 8 September 1991.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: North Macedonia (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: North Macedonia, independence (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Britannica gives 8 September 1991 for the independence vote)

declineSignals.value: Slow EU accession and emigration of young people have held the country back.

outcome.value: The Prespa agreement of June 2018 led to the name North Macedonia (constitutional change effective 12 February 2019); joined NATO in March 2020.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: North Macedonia (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: North Macedonia, independence (checked 15 Nov 2026) (the Prespa Agreement was announced in June 2018 and the name change took effect on 12 February 2019)

overallCertainty.value: Some history is disputed with neighbours.
